bug_semantics: asbplayer loads user-supplied subtitle files and, when the SubtitleHtml.render setting is on, leaves markup in cue text. SubtitleReader._filterText only optionally calls _decodeHTML (innerHTML-then-textContent strip) when subtitleHtml===remove; it performed no sanitization on the render path. Cue text is then interpolated unescaped into the video overlay via subtitle-controller._buildTextHtml → element-overlay innerHTML, and into the subtitle list via React dangerouslySetInnerHTML. A crafted .srt with HTML such as <script><button onmouseover=...> is therefore executed in the hosting streaming-site origin after the user loads the file with render-HTML enabled. Default remains SubtitleHtml.remove, so the setting is part of the UI:R path. This is stored XSS (CWE-79), not unrestricted upload/RCE; NVD later corrected the English description from file-upload RCE to XSS while leaving CWE-434.
flaw_origin: The XSS became reachable for .srt in 209fe85c993ed525a41dedce57cf146999350d71 (2025-03-29 author / 2025-04-06 committer): it added SubtitleHtml.render, changed SRT/VTT parsing from always _filterText(text, true) to a setting-gated _removeXml, and switched SubtitlePlayer from escaped React text children to dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Immediate parent 8a759859620a184bd4f6bd8fadef475ec28f4d30 always stripped SRT/VTT HTML in _filterText and rendered list text as {subtitle.text}. Overlay innerHTML interpolation already existed, but SRT HTML could not survive into that sink until this commit. No sanitizer was added until 65f0cdce0579dbcb1a25f24f8743fabac45606c6 (PR #905, first in v1.15.0).

reasoning: CVE-2025-69771 / GHSA-47p7-hmcr-q3rr is a real, published XSS, not a withdrawn advisory. MITRE/NVD describe crafted .srt HTML executing in the streaming-site origin; the tistory writeup names _filterText/_decodeHTML and an onmouseover button PoC; maintainer PR #905 reproduces the same SRT+render-HTML path. The NVD CWE-434/file-upload wording is a mis-tag of that XSS, not a false positive. Before 209fe85c, SRT/VTT cues were always HTML-stripped in _filterText(..., true) via _decodeHTML, and the subtitle list used escaped React text, so the reported .srt payload could not remain live markup. 209fe85c is the smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable lines: optional skip of that strip plus dangerouslySetInnerHTML of cue text, feeding the pre-existing overlay innerHTML sink. Immediate parent 8a759859 is present and was inspected; the render setting, unforced SRT strip, and dangerouslySetInnerHTML are absent there. The commit is not a merge or reconstructable squash aggregate. Fix 65f0cdce (PR #905) adds DOMPurify.sanitize in _filterText, is missing from v1.13.0/v1.14.0, and first tags at v1.15.0, matching the writeup's <=1.14.0 window.
